# nodo-mcp

> Six signed GETs against NODO's list of yield-bearing assets, loans against them, and lending-market rates.

Read [src/sign.ts](src/sign.ts) first. The signature is Ed25519 over six newline-joined lines: `nodo-workload-v2`, the api key, a unix expiry 30 seconds ahead, `GET`, `pathname + search` of the fetched URL (including `/api/v2`), and the SHA-256 hex of an empty body. A refused read is often HTTP 200 whose only key is `error`.

Some assets pay a yield. Tokenized government debt and private credit are common examples. The same asset can be posted as collateral and borrowed against, usually in dollars. The extra return is real only when the asset pays more than the loan costs, the loan stays short of the point where the collateral is sold, and the figures are from today.

A neobank comparing assets, a holder comparing loans, and another project showing these markets all read the same list. NODO keeps that list current and publishes it at https://app.nodo.xyz/api/v2. NODO does not hold the money. This repository only reads the list. Preparing a loan stays on the API.

English is the default. [中文](llms.zh.txt) · [日本語](llms.ja.txt)

## How to look something up

- [Yield-bearing assets and loans against them](skills/find-nodo-yield/SKILL.md): what an asset pays, and what is left after interest
- [Lending markets and rate history](skills/read-nodo-markets/SKILL.md): which market takes the collateral, when the loan would be closed out, and what the market has charged

## What a caller can ask

- `list_assets`, then `get_asset`: the assets, their yield, their size, and their terms
- `list_opportunities`, then `get_opportunity`: one asset in one market, the yield after interest, and the largest loan short of the point where the collateral is sold
- `list_markets`: the markets, narrowed by name, collateral, or the asset borrowed
- `get_market_apy_history`: what a market has paid, and what it has cost to borrow

Lists return about ten rows unless a larger page is requested. `nextOffset` marks the next page. `asOfTime` is when the figures were read.
